key_gap: The AI produced a complete, feasible 5-stream conference plan and matched the dependency machinery, but its level-1 outline was logistics-heavy and reached on-site safety/emergency/accessibility only via a second coverage sweep, it did not compute the critical-path duration and float as a designed artifact (1 week of float emerged only in REVIEW), and the merge-back step (run-of-show, budget roll-up, single source of truth) was present but less deliberate than the human's designed integration pass. The human's clause-to-stream coverage mapping, explicit edge list, and critical-path + float arithmetic are the decomposition-defining moves the AI reached later or partially.
learning_signal: On large multi-part goals, decomposition completeness is checkable and the human style's edge is its machinery: (1) map every clause of the stated goal to a level-1 stream before deepening (completeness gate), (2) recurse until every leaf has an owner class and a <= 2-week duration, (3) name dependencies as explicit edges with a computed critical path and float, and (4) design the integration step (merge-back: run-of-show, budget roll-up, single source of truth) as a first-class component rather than an afterthought. The AI's first sweep under-covered safety/accessibility and its float was a REVIEW discovery, showing it treats coverage and integration as checks rather than as design-time artifacts.
suggested_improvement: Extend the WHAT-stage default frame for multi-part planning goals to mandate a clause-to-stream coverage matrix as a gate artifact (any goal clause with no claiming stream blocks progression), and require the plan deliverable to state the critical-path duration with float and a named integration/merge-back step before selection; treat 'coverage sweep found a new area' in REVIEW as a process miss, not a success.

key_gap: The human style partitioned four simultaneous service alerts into four sub-problems and spent 38 minutes on internally consistent per-service checks that could not converge, because the cross-cutting cause (a 01:50 shared-config change rotating the connection string to an under-provisioned replica) lives outside every sub-problem's boundary; the simultaneity signal visible in the first screen of data was treated as noise. The AI won by posing 'one cause or many?' at WHAT with a falsifiable signal (simultaneity across independent services => shared substrate), running the cheap config/deploy diff first, and resolving at T=18 vs T+47.
learning_signal: Before decomposing any multi-symptom operational problem, run a cross-cutting scan: do the symptoms co-occur in time and share a substrate (config/deploy/DB/cache/mesh)? If yes, the shared-cause hypothesis must be tested first; decomposition is then reserved for a bounded confirmation sweep after the fix, not for the primary diagnosis. A stop rule for the style's failure: if all sub-problems individually 'pass' but the goal is unmet, the cause is outside the decomposition — re-check the whole-level signal before going deeper.
suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory WHAT-stage 'cross-cutting scan' for multi-symptom time-boxed problems: (1) check simultaneity and common substrate before any per-symptom sub-plan; (2) record a one-cause-vs-many hypothesis with its falsifier and order diagnostics by information-per-minute (the cheap diff first); (3) use per-symptom checks only post-fix as a bounded confirmation sweep; and add the stop rule 'sub-problems pass but the goal is unmet => the cause is outside the decomposition' as a REVIEW check.
